signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed Divergence
signals.text: USD outperforms the G10 basket with a 1W average of +1.213% across 9 pairs, while NOK lags at −1.106% across 2 pairs, generating a critical 2.319% leader-laggard divergence. Fed holds at 4.0%. On the technical side, USD/NOK trades above its SMA20 at 9.311, with the SMA50 at 9.459 capping immediate extensions. With VIX at 15.4 reflecting normal volatility, broad cross-asset conditions favor sustained yield-driven dispersion over defensive positioning. The acute performance gap confirms strong capital flows favoring USD assets over high-beta commodity currencies. Trade bias: Long USD/NOK; policy divergence and bilateral spread expansion favor upside momentum. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy meeting 24 Sep. Risk: Norges Bank delivers an unexpectedly hawkish policy update, narrowing the bilateral spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — CB Surprise Repricing + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades higher at 157.06 following the Bank of Japan rate increase to 1.25% in a split decision. The policy action failed to stem currency weakness as Governor Ueda signaled that trend inflation will only sustainably reach the 2% target around late FY2026 into FY2027. Nominal policy rates of Fed 4.0% vs BoJ 1.25% maintain a 275bp advantage favoring the dollar, while SOFR at 3.62% vs TONA at 0.98% keeps a +264bp OIS carry differential firmly in place. However, Saxo Bank 1M 25d risk reversals show a pronounced put skew of −2.08, indicating heavy demand for downside protection despite spot gains. Price trades below its SMA50 at 159.14 and SMA200 at 158.40, while remaining below the 160.00 threshold that previously triggered official verbal warnings. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; wide carry premium conflicts with elevated downside options hedging. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 30 Oct. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 escalates official intervention risk, accelerating downside options realization.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Crowded Long Unwind
signals.text: GBP speculative positioning sits in extended territory with CFTC Leveraged Funds holding net long +40,361 contracts, placing positioning at the 86th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +1.02. Weekly flow shows momentum stalling, as leveraged funds cut net length by −7,143 contracts WoW and −2,361 over 4 weeks. GBP/USD spot trades at 1.3372, breaking beneath its technical cluster including the SMA20 at 1.3532, SMA50 at 1.3482, and SMA200 at 1.3455. The policy backdrop remains balanced with Fed at 4.0% vs BoE at 3.75% providing a narrow 25bp carry advantage to the dollar. The combination of stalled speculative inflows and a break below all major moving averages marks an ongoing positioning unwind rather than an orderly pause. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; long liquidation drives downward momentum through moving-average support. Catalyst: BoE meeting 5 Nov. Risk: Leveraged funds resume net accumulation, driving spot back above the SMA200 at 1.3455.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Technical Resistance
signals.text: CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net long +48,379 contracts in AUD, placing positioning at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week historical range with a z-score of +1.72. RBA holds at 4.35%. AUD/USD trades at 0.7129, holding above its SMA50 at 0.7084 and SMA200 at 0.7013, but pinned below the SMA20 resistance at 0.7170. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment sits balanced at 50% long and 50% short, offering no contrarian cushion against an institutional unwind. With speculative long exposure near the upper boundary of its annual distribution, upside progress faces heavy positioning friction unless fresh policy catalysts emerge. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; crowded long positioning caps upside momentum into resistance. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep. Risk: Leveraged funds aggressively liquidate length below the SMA50 at 0.7084, triggering a broader trend reversal.
